newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW - Jusco to double group listings by 2000.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Jusco to double group listings by 2000.

text.p: Japanese supermarket operator Jusco Co Ltd plans to more than double the number of its group firms that are listed on domestic bourses to about 30 from the current 14 by the end of 2000.

"Although we had been aiming to increase the number of listed firms in our group to 20 before the end of this century, I think we can raise that to 30," Jusco chairman Takuya Okada said in an interview.
Jusco is a core company of the Aeon group, which comprises 150 firms in Japan and overseas.
Among the group's listed firms are convenience store operator Ministop Co Ltd and finance company Aeon Credit Service Co Ltd.
Okada said candidates for going public included Hokuriku Jusco Co Ltd, an operator of regional Jusco stores, Laura Ashley Japan Co Ltd and Talbots Japan Co Ltd.
Jusco has alliances with Britain's Laura Ashley Holdings Plc and U.S. firms Talbots Inc, as well as U.S. firms Sports Authority Inc and OfficeMax Inc.
Okada said the company would continue to seek tie-ups with overseas retailers.
Funds raised from the listing would be used mainly to enhance the international competitiveness of the group's specialty retailers, Okada said.
He said the company aims to increase group current profit to 200 billion yen within the next four to five years, compared with 70.1 billion yen in the last business year, which ended on February 28.

To weather intensifying competition amid industry deregulation, Okada said business emphasis would be placed on its large regional shopping centres, which serve around 400,000 people, as well as smaller-scale centres which comprise various specialty stores and discount stores.
Okada also said he was considering merging three of the group's household goods retailers -- Keiyo Co Ltd, Homac Corp and Home Wide Corp -- to achieve economies of scale.
